1. A rotorcraft with at least one main rotor and a fuselage, comprising:
a tail boom connected to the fuselage, the tail boom extending from the fuselage toward a duct-type portion;
a shroud provided at the duct-type portion and forming a transverse duct;
at least one ducted tail rotor rotatably arranged in the transverse duct, wherein the at least one ducted tail rotor comprises a plurality of rotor blades mounted to a rotatable rotor hub; and
a stator with a gearbox fairing mounted to the shroud for supporting the rotatable rotor hub in the transverse duct, wherein the stator comprises at least one rotatable stator blade connecting the gearbox fairing to the shroud.
2. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the at least one rotatable stator blade connects an outer surface of the gearbox fairing to an inner surface of the transverse duct.
3. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the at least one rotatable stator blade comprises a wing-like body with a wing-like aerodynamic profile comprising an aerodynamic center.
4. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the wing-like body is rotatable about a rotation axis that is spaced apart from the aerodynamic center.
5. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the wing-like body is rotatably mounted to a stationary strut forming the rotation axis.
6. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the wing-like body is rotatably mounted to the stationary strut via at least one bearing.
7. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the stationary strut rigidly attaches the gearbox fairing to the shroud.
8. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the wing-like body comprises a leading edge and a trailing edge, and wherein the rotation axis is arranged closer to the leading edge than the associated aerodynamic center.
9. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein a torsion spring connects the wing-like body to one of the gearbox fairing, the shroud, or the stationary strut.
10. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the torsion spring is mounted coaxially to the stationary strut.
11. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein an airfoil-like extension is provided at the trailing edge of the wing-like body.
12. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the airfoil-like extension and the wing- like body are configured to generate forces directed into diametrically opposed directions.
13. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the at least one rotatable stator blade rotates in response to an airflow induced pressure generated by an airflow acting on the at least one rotatable stator blade.
14. The rotorcraft of The rotorcraft of
wherein the at least one rotatable stator blade rotates into an operating position associated with reduced drag generation.
15. The rotorcraft o claim 1, which is embodied as a helicopter, wherein the tail boom extends in a longitudinal direction of the helicopter from the fuselage toward the duct-type portion, and wherein the at least one ducted tail rotor is rotatable in the transverse duct about an associated tail rotor rotation axis oriented at least
03BD0637/US essentially perpendicular to the longitudinal direction of the helicopter.
